# Reproducibility: Shared packages on shared servers {#repro}

On shared IAB servers, people typically work in teams on the same projects.
When `install.packages()` fails to install to `C:/...R/` (no admin rights), it falls back to your personal Documents folder on that server.
This means packages are both **user-specific** and **server-specific**, i.e, installed packages are only available to your account on that server.
This creates a critical reproducibility problem: each team member ends up with *different* package versions, and code may break across team members and even across servers for the same team member.

On shared servers, team members need access to _the same package versions_ for reproducible work. 
The most reliable solution is to use a project-specific `.Rprofile` that points all team members to a shared package library. Installation is only needed once per project[^rver] or at deliberate update points. When you join an existing project, skip all setup steps and go straight to [Using packages](#sharedlibrary).

[^rver]: As long as you're using the same R version.

**Best practice for team projects**

The following setup ensures that

- **Everyone** on the team works with **the same package versions**, as long as they use the same R version (major.minor)
- The setup **travels with your project**
- No manual setup needed when someone joins the project


0. Set up an [`.Rproj`](#rproj)
1. Create a `./prog/library/...` folder in your project root
2. Add a project-specific `.Rprofile` (use the [ToolsAB](https://github.webapp.dst.baintern.de/iab/ToolsAB/blob/master/Rprofiles/) template)
3. Install the `{fdzinstall}` package
4. Using `fdzinstall` now installs packages to the same folder:
   ```r
   fdzinstall("ggplot2")  # respects .libPaths() from .Rprofile
   ```
5. *Optional: use version control (git)*[^git]

[^git]: Only commit the `.Rprofile` (and `.Rproj`), not the `prog/library/` folder. Package binaries are large, platform-specific, and do not belong in a repository. Add `prog/library/` to your `.gitignore` instead, and make sure the library lives on a shared drive (e.g. `N:`) so that all team members see the same packages.

## Set up your project library (do this once)

#### Prerequisite {.unnumbered}

You're in your project directory with your `.Rproj` file. See the [`.Rproj`](#rproj) chapter for details.
You can check whether the (correct) `.Rproj` is active:

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rstudioapi::getActiveProject() 
```
:::


Now create a subfolder in your `prog` directory where all packages for this project will be stored.
Run each of these steps once:

#### Create the shared library folder {.unnumbered}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
libdir <- file.path("./prog/library", 
                    paste(getRversion()[[1, 1:2]], collapse = "-"))
dir.create(libdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```
:::


This will create a library specific to the R version you're currently using.

#### Download and edit the `.Rprofile` from [ToolsAB](https://github.webapp.dst.baintern.de/iab/ToolsAB/blob/master/Rprofiles/) {.unnumbered}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
download.file(
  url = "https://github.webapp.dst.baintern.de/iab/ToolsAB/raw/master/Rprofiles/iab_profile.R",
  destfile = ".Rprofile"
)
```
:::


Edit line 25 in the `.Rprofile` to change the library directory to a subfolder of your project, e.g. `"./prog/library"`:

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
libdir <- file.path("./prog/library", 
                    paste(getRversion()[[1, 1:2]], collapse = "-"))
```
:::


This will create a subfolder in `"./prog/library"` specific to the R version you're currently using - in our example, ./prog/library/4-5.

#### Restart R (`CTRL + F10`).  {.unnumbered}

#### Check the library path {.unnumbered}

After restarting R, verify that the project library is active:

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.libPaths()  # the first entry should point to ./prog/library/...
```
:::


#### Get `{fdzinstall}` from [ToolsAB](https://github.webapp.dst.baintern.de/iab/ToolsAB/) {.unnumbered} 

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
install.packages(
  "https://github.webapp.dst.baintern.de/iab/ToolsAB/raw/master/fdzinstall_R/fdzinstall_1.2.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL,
  type = "source"
)
```
:::



#### Install packages using `fdzinstall` {.unnumbered}

Agree with your team before installing or updating packages, since changes affect everyone who uses the shared library.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fdzinstall::fdzinstall("tidyverse")
```
:::


## Using packages {#sharedlibrary}

When anyone on your team opens the `.Rproj` file, the `.Rprofile` sets the same library path and `library()` loads packages from the shared folder.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
```
:::


After (re-)starting R, you might want to verify that the shared project library is active:

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
.libPaths()  # the first entry should point to ./prog/library/...
```
:::
